## 12,781 Bikes

*November 2026*

Every Santander bike in London has a five digit number painted on the frame, and the website remembers which one you took on every single ride. I have been riding them since July. TfL is replacing the whole system on November 17th, so before it went I copied my history out: 201 rides. TfL also publishes every trip anyone takes, bike number included, which means I can draw the whole fleet. Here it is: 12,781 bikes, one tile each, in number order with the e-bikes last. Darker tiles get ridden more by the rest of London. The lit ones are the 178 I have caught so far. I would like to catch them all.

**There is a bike number 4.** It is the first tile. The lowest numbers in London are 4, 6 and 9, the highest is 99985, and 87% of five digit numbers belong to no bike at all. Bike 4 did 181 rides in four months. I have not caught it.

**Nobody wants the old bikes.** The pale rows at the top are the bikes numbered below 50,000. They are 24% of the fleet but get 17% of London's rides, and 11% of mine. My guess is that they are the older ones, with the old seat latch, which is worse.

**The busiest bike in London does 4.6 rides a day.** That is bike 57283, with 549 rides in four months. The best I have caught is 57863 (471 rides, busier than 99% of the fleet). The other extreme is e-bike 60162, which shows up exactly once in four months of London's data. Then I got it. On average my bikes are a little busier than London's (248 rides against 234), which they have to be: a bike that gets around more is easier to run into. And London does not pick its bikes at random either: if it did, this histogram would be a Poisson spike six times narrower. Press the button.

**No bike has a neighbourhood.** For each bike I measured how far its docks spread from the centre of its own travels. The typical bike roams 4.0 km, and half of all bikes fall between 3.8 and 4.2. Among bikes with at least 50 rides, the biggest homebody is 59145 at 2.3 km and the widest roamer is 30064 at 5.5. Sort the grid by roaming and my catches land everywhere.

**I pick bikes the way horses kick Prussians.** The Poisson distribution describes rare, random events, and it was made famous in 1898 by counting Prussian cavalrymen kicked to death by their horses. If I pick bikes at random, each bike has been picked $$\lambda = 180 / 12{,}781 \approx 0.014$$ times on average, and the chance that a given bike has been caught exactly k times is

$$P(k) = \frac{\lambda^k e^{-\lambda}}{k!}$$

Multiply by 12,781 bikes and that is 177.5 caught once and 1.2 caught twice. I have 176 and 2. (Picks, not rides: 21 times I parked a bike, came back later, and it was still there. Those are not picks.)

**It took 107 picks to get the same bike twice.** The two yellow tiles are the bikes I have caught twice. The first was 56462. I only took it on Aug 12 because the bike before it lasted 4 seconds, and 32 days later it turned up again. This is the birthday problem: a room needs only 23 people for an even chance that two of them share a birthday, and a fleet of 12,781 bikes needs only 134 picks. Mine came on pick 107, which is like a room of 19 getting lucky.

**Two coincidences are enough to count every bike in London.** Run the birthday problem backwards and you get how biologists count the fish in a lake: catch some, tag them, throw them back, and see how many turn up again. Any two picks have a 1 in N chance of being the same bike, and n picks make n(n-1)/2 pairs, so the number of coincidences I should expect is

$$\frac{n(n-1)}{2N}$$

I have had 2 in 180 picks, so

$$N \approx \frac{ 180 \times 179 }{2 \times 2 } = 8{,}055$$

The real answer is 12,781. Two fish is thin evidence (the honest range is 2,000 to 67,000), and the count runs low for the same reason it does in lakes: not every fish is equally easy to catch. See the old bikes.

**Half the e-bike numbers do not exist.** The blue block is the e-bikes. I have caught 19, numbered from 60162 to 64182. In World War II the Allies estimated German tank production from the serial numbers of captured tanks, and the same sum here says about 4,467 e-bike numbers. The real span is 4,119. But only 2,151 of those numbers are on an actual bike. The method counts serial numbers, not tanks.

**My bikes cheat on me.** I have ridden 178 bikes 201 times. In the same 115 days, going by their February to May habits, those bikes were ridden about 42,000 times by other people. That is 210 rides with someone else for every ride with me. Bike 56462 at least came back.

**My next reunion is due on December 21st.** Every pick now has a 1.4% chance of being a bike I already have, so the next reunion should take about 72 picks, which at 1.6 picks a day is 46 days. There is a 71% chance of at least one before New Year. I will report back.

**I will be done in the year 2250.** Catching every bike is the coupon collector's problem, and it is slow for a cruel reason: the more bikes I have, the more often I pick one I already caught. At 1.6 picks a day, half the fleet takes 16 years and all of it takes 224. The last bike alone takes 22 years.

11;62800|e|Sep 24 (2 rides);62855|e|Sep 19;63186|e|Sep 12;63206|e|Sep 27;63209|e|Oct 17 (2 rides);64182|e|Sep 20";
  var roamRaw = "";
  var COLS = 113, CELL = 12, GAP = 2, N_PEDAL = 10630, HIST_MAX = 550, MEAN_RIDES = 233.75;
  var colors = { p: 'hsl(5, 70%, 52%)', e: 'hsl(195, 75%, 36%)', y: 'hsl(46, 90%, 55%)' };
  var names = { p: 'Caught', e: 'Caught', y: 'Caught twice' };

  function numbers(s) {
    var out = [], n = 0;
    for (var i = 0; i < s.length; i++) {
      if (s[i] === '~') { n += parseInt(s.substr(i + 1, 4), 36); i += 4; }
      else n += parseInt(s[i], 36);
      out.push(n);
    }
    return out;
  }
  // One entry per bike: number order, e-bikes last.
  var nums = numbers(dPedal).concat(numbers(dEbike));
  var count = nums.map(function (_, i) { return parseInt(countsRaw.substr(i * 2, 2), 36); });
  var roam = nums.map(function (_, i) { return parseInt(roamRaw.substr(i * 2, 2), 36) / 100; });   // km
  var mine = {};
  mineRaw.split(';').forEach(function (s) {
    var f = s.split('|');
    mine[f[0]] = { cat: f[1], when: f[2] };
  });

  function shade(b) {
    var t = Math.min(1, count[b] / 450);
    return b < N_PEDAL
      ? 'hsl(35, ' + (30 + 10 * t) + '%, ' + (93 - 17 * t) + '%)'
      : 'hsl(195, ' + (25 + 30 * t) + '%, ' + (90 - 14 * t) + '%)';
  }

  // ---- the grid -------------------------------------------------------------
  var byNumber = nums.map(function (_, i) { return i; });
  // Every sort keeps the pedal bikes and the e-bikes in their own blocks.
  function sorted(by) {
    function cmp(a, b) { return by[b] - by[a] || a - b; }
    return byNumber.slice(0, N_PEDAL).sort(cmp).concat(byNumber.slice(N_PEDAL).sort(cmp));
  }
  // A bike with a handful of rides has no meaningful spread, so those go last.
  var roamKey = roam.map(function (km, b) { return count[b] >= 50 ? km : km / 1000 - 1; });
  var SORTS = {
    number: { pos: byNumber, first: 'lowest number', mid: '', last: 'e-bikes last' },
    busy: { pos: sorted(count), first: 'busiest pedal bike', mid: 'each colour runs busiest to quietest', last: 'quietest e-bike' },
    roam: { pos: sorted(roamKey), first: 'widest roaming pedal bike', mid: 'each colour runs wanderer to homebody', last: 'then the barely ridden' }
  };
  var pos = byNumber;                       // tile position -> bike
  var canvas = document.getElementById('bikes-grid');
  var ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');

  function draw() {
    ctx.fillStyle = '#fff8ef';
    ctx.fillRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
    var lit = [];
    pos.forEach(function (b, i) {
      var x = (i % COLS) * CELL, y = Math.floor(i / COLS) * CELL, m = mine[nums[b]];
      if (m) { lit.push([x, y, m.cat]); return; }
      ctx.fillStyle = shade(b);
      ctx.fillRect(x, y, CELL - GAP, CELL - GAP);
    });
    // Lit tiles fill their whole cell, drawn last so nothing paints over them.
    lit.forEach(function (t) {
      ctx.fillStyle = colors[t[2]];
      ctx.fillRect(t[0] - GAP / 2, t[1] - GAP / 2, CELL, CELL);
    });
    // The two yellow tiles get a ring so they can be found.
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#4a5a4f';
    ctx.lineWidth = 3;
    lit.forEach(function (t) {
      if (t[2] === 'y') ctx.strokeRect(t[0] - GAP / 2 - 5, t[1] - GAP / 2 - 5, CELL + 10, CELL + 10);
    });
  }
  draw();

  var sortButtons = document.querySelectorAll('.bikes-sort button[data-sort]');
  var firstLabel = document.getElementById('bikes-first');
  var midLabel = document.getElementById('bikes-mid');
  var lastLabel = document.getElementById('bikes-last');
  function sortBy(key) {
    var sort = SORTS[key];
    pos = sort.pos;
    for (var i = 0; i < sortButtons.length; i++) {
      sortButtons[i].setAttribute('aria-pressed', sortButtons[i].getAttribute('data-sort') === key ? 'true' : 'false');
    }
    firstLabel.textContent = '\u2196 ' + sort.first;
    midLabel.textContent = sort.mid;
    lastLabel.textContent = sort.last + ' \u2198';
    hideTooltip();
    draw();
  }
  for (var i = 0; i < sortButtons.length; i++) {
    sortButtons[i].addEventListener('click', function () { sortBy(this.getAttribute('data-sort')); });
  }

  var tooltip = document.getElementById('bikes-tooltip');

  function bikeAt(clientX, clientY) {
    var rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
    var col = Math.floor((clientX - rect.left) * (canvas.width / rect.width) / CELL);
    var row = Math.floor((clientY - rect.top) * (canvas.height / rect.height) / CELL);
    var i = row * COLS + col;
    return col >= 0 && col < COLS && row >= 0 && i < pos.length ? pos[i] : -1;
  }

  function line(cls, text) {
    var d = document.createElement('div');
    if (cls) d.className = cls;
    d.textContent = text;
    return d;
  }

  function showTooltip(b, clientX, clientY) {
    var n = nums[b], m = mine[n], rides = count[b];
    while (tooltip.firstChild) tooltip.removeChild(tooltip.firstChild);
    var head = line('bikes-tip-name', '');
    var sw = document.createElement('span');
    sw.className = 'bikes-swatch';
    sw.style.background = m ? colors[m.cat] : shade(b);
    head.appendChild(sw);
    head.appendChild(document.createTextNode('Bike ' + n + (b >= N_PEDAL ? ' (e-bike)' : '')));
    tooltip.appendChild(head);
    tooltip.appendChild(line('', rides + (rides === 1 ? ' ride' : ' rides') + ' by London, Feb to May'));
    if (roam[b] > 0) tooltip.appendChild(line('', 'Roams ' + roam[b].toFixed(1) + ' km'));
    tooltip.appendChild(line(m ? '' : 'bikes-tip-dim', m ? names[m.cat] + ': ' + m.when : 'Not caught yet'));
    tooltip.style.display = 'block';
    var tw = 208, th = tooltip.offsetHeight + 4;
    var left = clientX + 14, top = clientY + 14;
    if (left + tw > window.innerWidth) left = Math.max(4, clientX - 14 - tw);
    if (top + th > window.innerHeight) top = clientY - 14 - th;
    tooltip.style.left = left + 'px';
    tooltip.style.top = top + 'px';
  }

  function hideTooltip() {
    tooltip.style.display = 'none';
  }

  canvas.addEventListener('mousemove', function (e) {
    var b = bikeAt(e.clientX, e.clientY);
    if (b >= 0) showTooltip(b, e.clientX, e.clientY); else hideTooltip();
  });
  canvas.addEventListener('mouseleave', hideTooltip);
  canvas.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
    var b = bikeAt(e.clientX, e.clientY);
    if (b >= 0) { showTooltip(b, e.clientX, e.clientY); e.stopPropagation(); } else hideTooltip();
  });
  document.addEventListener('click', hideTooltip);
  window.addEventListener('scroll', hideTooltip, { passive: true });

  // ---- the histogram: every bike by how busy it is, my catches as ticks -------
  var hist = document.getElementById('bikes-hist');
  var hx = hist.getContext('2d');
  var BIN = 10, NBINS = HIST_MAX / BIN, RUG = 70, W = hist.width, H = hist.height - RUG, bw = W / NBINS;
  var bins = [], equal = [];
  for (var k = 0; k < NBINS; k++) { bins.push(0); equal.push(0); }
  count.forEach(function (c) { bins[Math.min(NBINS - 1, Math.floor(c / BIN))]++; });
  // If every ride went to a random bike, rides per bike would be Poisson with the same mean.
  var pk = Math.exp(-MEAN_RIDES);
  for (var r = 0; r < HIST_MAX; r++) {
    if (r > 0) pk *= MEAN_RIDES / r;
    equal[Math.floor(r / BIN)] += pk * nums.length;
  }

  function drawHist(showEqual) {
    var tallest = Math.max.apply(null, showEqual ? equal : bins);
    hx.fillStyle = 'hsl(35, 45%, 91%)';
    hx.fillRect(0, 0, W, hist.height);
    bins.forEach(function (n, k) {
      var t = Math.min(1, (k + 0.5) * BIN / 450), h = (H - 10) * n / tallest;
      hx.fillStyle = 'hsl(35, ' + (30 + 10 * t) + '%, ' + (86 - 22 * t) + '%)';
      hx.fillRect(k * bw, H - h, bw - GAP, h);
    });
    if (showEqual) {
      hx.fillStyle = 'rgba(74, 90, 79, 0.85)';
      equal.forEach(function (n, k) {
        var h = (H - 10) * n / tallest;
        if (h >= 1) hx.fillRect(k * bw, H - h, bw - GAP, h);
      });
    }
    hx.globalAlpha = 0.75;
    nums.forEach(function (n, b) {
      var m = mine[n];
      if (!m) return;
      hx.fillStyle = colors[m.cat];
      hx.fillRect(W * count[b] / HIST_MAX - 2, H + 14, 4, RUG - 28);
    });
    hx.globalAlpha = 1;
  }
  drawHist(false);

  var equalButton = document.getElementById('bikes-equal');
  equalButton.addEventListener('click', function () {
    var on = equalButton.getAttribute('aria-pressed') !== 'true';
    equalButton.setAttribute('aria-pressed', on ? 'true' : 'false');
    drawHist(on);
  });
})();
</script>
